questions.title: First Greeting Printer
questions.description:
A brand-new Ruby learner wants their first program: read a name from stdin and print a friendly greeting.

Input Format:
A single line containing a person's name.

Output Format:
A single line: Hello, <name>!

Constraints:
Name is 1 to 30 characters, contains only letters and spaces.
questions.sourcecode:
name = gets.chomp
puts "Hello, #{name}!"

questions.title: Two Number Sum
questions.description:
Practice running a Ruby script: read two integers and print their sum.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated integers.

Output Format:
A single line with the integer sum.

Constraints:
-1000 <= a, b <= 1000.
questions.sourcecode:
a, b = gets.split.map(&:to_i)
puts a + b

questions.title: Double the Number
questions.description:
A drill for the Ruby interpreter: read one integer and print double its value.

Input Format:
A single integer on one line.

Output Format:
A single integer: 2 * n.

Constraints:
-500 <= n <= 500.
questions.sourcecode:
n = gets.to_i
puts n * 2

questions.title: String Length Reporter
questions.description:
Pretend you are inside IRB exploring Ruby. Read a word and report its character count.

Input Format:
A single line containing a word (no spaces).

Output Format:
A single integer: the number of characters.

Constraints:
1 <= word length <= 100.
questions.sourcecode:
word = gets.chomp
puts word.length

questions.title: Cube Calculator
questions.description:
A starter Ruby script: read an integer and print its cube (n * n * n).

Input Format:
A single integer on one line.

Output Format:
A single integer: n^3.

Constraints:
-20 <= n <= 20.
questions.sourcecode:
n = gets.to_i
puts n * n * n

questions.title: Echo Three Times
questions.description:
Read a short message and print it on three separate lines, exactly as IRB drills repetition.

Input Format:
A single line with a short message.

Output Format:
Three lines, each containing the message.

Constraints:
1 <= message length <= 50.
questions.sourcecode:
msg = gets.chomp
3.times { puts msg }

questions.title: Bookstore Receipt Printer
questions.description:
A neighborhood bookstore uses a tiny Ruby script for receipts. Given a book title, quantity and unit price (integers), print one summary line.

Input Format:
Three lines: title, quantity (integer), unit price (integer rupees).

Output Format:
One line: Total for <qty> copies of <title>: <total>

Constraints:
1 <= qty <= 100, 1 <= price <= 10000, title length 1 to 40.
questions.sampleoutput1: Total for 3 copies of Ruby Programming: 1497
questions.output1: Total for 5 copies of Rails Way: 1500
questions.output3: Total for 10 copies of Matz Book: 1500
questions.sourcecode:
title = gets.chomp
qty = gets.to_i
price = gets.to_i
total = qty * price
puts "Total for #{qty} copies of #{title}: #{total}"

questions.title: Coffee Shop Table Assigner
questions.description:
A cafe manager runs a Ruby script at the entrance. Read a customer's name and a free table number; print a welcome line.

Input Format:
Two lines: name and table number (integer).

Output Format:
One line: Welcome, <name>! Your table is <table>.

Constraints:
1 <= name length <= 30, 1 <= table <= 99.
questions.sourcecode:
name = gets.chomp
table = gets.to_i
puts "Welcome, #{name}! Your table is #{table}."

questions.title: Garden Row Calculator
questions.description:
A gardener is writing a Ruby script to plan planting. Read total plants and plants-per-row (both integers, per_row divides total evenly); print how many rows are needed.

Input Format:
Two lines: total plants and plants per row.

Output Format:
One line: You need <rows> rows.

Constraints:
1 <= per_row <= 50, total is a multiple of per_row, 1 <= total <= 5000.
questions.sourcecode:
total = gets.to_i
per_row = gets.to_i
rows = total / per_row
puts "You need #{rows} rows."

questions.title: Marathon Pace Banner
questions.description:
A marathon organizer prints a pace banner. Read the race distance in km and the runner's time in hours (both integers, distance divides hours evenly). Print km-per-hour as an integer.

Input Format:
Two lines: distance_km and time_hours.

Output Format:
One line: Pace banner: <pace> km per hour.

Constraints:
1 <= distance, time <= 1000, distance divisible by time.
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= distance, time <= 1000, distance divisible by time
questions.sourcecode:
distance = gets.to_i
time = gets.to_i
pace = distance / time
puts "Pace banner: #{pace} km per hour."

questions.title: Countdown Launcher
questions.description:
A rocket-launch simulator counts down from n to 1, then announces liftoff. You must use a while loop (the countdown iterator helpers are disabled).

Input Format:
A single integer n.

Output Format:
One line: space-separated numbers from n down to 1, followed by Liftoff!
Example for n=5: 5 4 3 2 1 Liftoff!

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000.
questions.sourcecode:
n = gets.to_i
out = []
i = n
while i >= 1
  out << i
  i -= 1
end
puts out.join(" ") + " Liftoff!"

questions.title: Staircase Builder
questions.description:
An ASCII-art staircase has n steps. Line i contains i asterisk characters. Use a while loop to build each line character-by-character.

Input Format:
A single integer n.

Output Format:
Exactly n lines. Line i (1-indexed) has i asterisks, no trailing spaces.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50.
questions.sourcecode:
n = gets.to_i
i = 1
while i <= n
  line = ""
  j = 1
  while j <= i
    line += "*"
    j += 1
  end
  puts line
  i += 1
end

questions.title: Digit Sum Loop
questions.description:
A checksum utility computes the sum of decimal digits of a non-negative integer using a while loop (the digits helper is disabled).

Input Format:
A single non-negative integer.

Output Format:
A single integer: the sum of digits.

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 10^9.
questions.sourcecode:
n = gets.to_i
total = 0
while n > 0
  total += n % 10
  n /= 10
end
puts total

questions.title: Repeated Word Banner
questions.description:
A banner printer concatenates a word n times without using the multiplication operator or the times iterator.

Input Format:
Two lines: the word, then the integer count n.

Output Format:
A single line: the word repeated n times.

Constraints:
1 <= word length <= 20, 1 <= n <= 100.
questions.sourcecode:
word = gets.chomp
n = gets.to_i
out = ""
i = 0
while i < n
  out += word
  i += 1
end
puts out

questions.title: Power Loop Calculator
questions.description:
A math utility computes b raised to e (b^e) for non-negative exponents using a while loop. The exponent operator and the times iterator are disabled.

Input Format:
Two lines: base b and exponent e (non-negative integers).

Output Format:
A single integer: b^e.

Constraints:
0 <= b <= 100, 0 <= e <= 15, b^e fits in 64-bit integer.
questions.sourcecode:
b = gets.to_i
e = gets.to_i
result = 1
i = 0
while i < e
  result = result * b
  i += 1
end
puts result

questions.title: Multiplication Table Row
questions.description:
A teacher prints the nth row of the multiplication table (n x 1 .. n x 10) using a while loop. The times, upto, each iterators are disabled.

Input Format:
A single integer n.

Output Format:
One line with ten space-separated products: n*1 n*2 ... n*10.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100.
questions.sourcecode:
n = gets.to_i
results = []
i = 1
while i <= 10
  results << (n * i)
  i += 1
end
puts results.join(" ")

questions.title: Primality Trial Loop
questions.description:
A number-theory demo classifies a non-negative integer as prime or composite using trial division with a while loop. The Prime library and higher-order iterators are disabled.

Input Format:
A single integer n.

Output Format:
A single word: prime or composite.
Note: 0 and 1 are composite; 2 and 3 are prime.

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 10^6.
questions.sourcecode:
n = gets.to_i
if n < 2
  puts "composite"
else
  is_p = true
  i = 2
  while i * i <= n
    if n % i == 0
      is_p = false
      break
    end
    i += 1
  end
  puts is_p ? "prime" : "composite"
end

questions.title: Collatz Sequence Printer
questions.description:
Print the Collatz (3n+1) sequence starting from a positive integer n, ending at 1. Use a while loop. Higher-order iterators are disabled.

Rule: if n is even, next = n/2; else next = 3*n + 1. Stop when n == 1.

Input Format:
A single integer n.

Output Format:
One line: space-separated sequence from n down to 1.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000.
questions.sourcecode:
n = gets.to_i
seq = [n]
while n != 1
  if n % 2 == 0
    n = n / 2
  else
    n = 3 * n + 1
  end
  seq << n
end
puts seq.join(" ")

questions.title: Binary Representation Builder
questions.description:
Convert a non-negative integer to its binary representation (as a string of 0/1, most-significant bit first) using a while loop. The built-in to_s with base argument is disabled.

Input Format:
A single non-negative integer.

Output Format:
A single line containing the binary representation (no leading zeros, except for input 0 which prints "0").

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 10^9.
questions.sourcecode:
n = gets.to_i
if n == 0
  puts "0"
else
  bits = []
  m = n
  while m > 0
    bits << (m % 2)
    m = m / 2
  end
  out = ""
  i = bits.length - 1
  while i >= 0
    out += "#{bits[i]}"
    i -= 1
  end
  puts out
end

questions.title: Euclidean GCD Loop
questions.description:
Compute the greatest common divisor of two positive integers using Euclid's algorithm with a while loop. The built-in gcd method and higher-order iterators are disabled.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated positive integers a and b.

Output Format:
A single integer: gcd(a, b).

Constraints:
1 <= a, b <= 10^9.
questions.sourcecode:
a, b = gets.split.map(&:to_i)
while b != 0
  temp = b
  b = a % b
  a = temp
end
puts a
